clue.text: Stonework produced by girl carrying child

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the child inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A girl with a baby in her arms somehow produces a piece of masonry.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is building work done in dressed stone, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Do one's share, putting up with family

definitions.meaning: pitch in and help with the work
sharing living quarters with others, as when lodging with relatives

explanation.surface: Doing your part while staying with relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to share tasks and to share accommodation.

clue.text: Give information and reveal just one thing

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing to the police
to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Inform and disclose only a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give information' sounds innocent but means to grass, as a criminal informer does.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a single item, especially one card alone in its suit.

clue.text: To develop business contacts, new serviceman has introduced a couple

indicators.note: the serviceman takes the couple into his midst

parts.note: erk is British slang for an aircraftman of the RAF
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A fresh recruit makes connections by introducing a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To network is to build professional contacts, an exact verbal synonym.

clue.text: Racy rogue's prepared address

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive s gives no letter

explanation.surface: A naughty scoundrel's speech is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a speech but is a form of address.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the formal way to address a duke or archbishop.

clue.text: African his room needs refurbishment

indicators.note: a room in need of refurbishment will be rearranged, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: An African man's room is in need of doing up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moors were North African people, so Moorish describes something African.

clue.text: Copper possibly had an encounter with gangster

parts.note: met means had an encounter
Al Capone was a notorious gangster

explanation.surface: A policeman ran into a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the element, an example of a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is one example of a metal, hence possibly.

clue.text: Out of condition, almost sickly-looking -but not in the rush hour

parts.note: off means unwell or out of sorts

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: peaky is British for looking pale and unwell

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell and pale but not in the busy commuting time.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak describes travel outside the busiest periods such as rush hour.

clue.text: Meet with popular scoundrel

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a cur is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: Meeting a well-liked villain.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost is to meet with or suffer it.

clue.text: They ride out to get what's coming to them

indicators.note: out signals the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: They ride off to claim what they are owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Heredity is what is passed down to one from ancestors, inheritance coming to them.

clue.text: Put up with limit after I left for university

indicators.note: the letter I leaves and the university's letter takes its place

parts.note: to constrict is to limit or restrict

explanation.surface: Someone tolerating restrictions after quitting for university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link word; swapping the I in CONSTRICT for U gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To construct a building is to put it up, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Tool causing a sudden problem

definitions.meaning: a cutting tool that smooths a surface flat
an unexpected difficulty that confronts one, as a blow in the face

explanation.surface: A piece of equipment that suddenly creates trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing a' simply links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from facing: a facing tool on a lathe, and a blow or obstacle met head-on.

clue.text: American serviceman sent back to smallest room in White House

indicators.note: a person sent back is turned around, so the serviceman's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: GI is the familiar term for a US soldier
the smallest room is a jocular British euphemism for the toilet, the loo

explanation.surface: A US soldier is returned to the toilet in the president's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' looks like the President's home, but it is a house made of white snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped shelter built of snow blocks, literally a white house.

clue.text: Gordon led astray, making a bloomer

indicators.note: letters gone astray have wandered out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Gordon was misled and made a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a mistake but here means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a yellow-flowered plant, and anything that blooms can be called a bloomer.

clue.text: Some drivers do remain inconspicuous

definitions.meaning: people who drive may sit behind someone else rather than at the front
keep out of the limelight and let others lead

explanation.surface: Certain motorists stay unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to accept a less prominent role, from sitting in a car's rear seat.

clue.text: Genuine article accepted by family member in charge

indicators.note: the family member takes the article inside

parts.note: an aunt is a family member
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A real item taken by a relative who is in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means real or not fake, a direct synonym of genuine.

clue.text: Confused? Go to Ely, my original source

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Puzzled? Go to the cathedral city of Ely, where I come from.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Etymology is a word's origin and history, its original source.

clue.text: Stop making reptile cross

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
cross means angry, irate

explanation.surface: Halt the angry snake.
explanation.walkthrough: In phonetics a stop is a consonant; an aspirate is a breathed one, the h sound.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics both terms name consonant sounds; an aspirate is a breathed consonant classed with stops.

clue.text: Dispatched to island, people correspond in mawkish fashion

parts.note: dispatched means sent
men are people
to tally is to agree or correspond

explanation.surface: Folk sent off to an island write each other soppy letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspond' suggests letter-writing, but here it means to match up.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means overly sentimental, so in mawkish fashion is the adverb of that feeling.

clue.text: Monks are suitable

definitions.meaning: monks belong to a religious community

explanation.surface: Monks are appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks are members of a religious order; the phrase also means fitting or correct.

clue.text: A match for Venus

definitions.meaning: an old name for a friction match
the planet seen as the morning star

explanation.surface: A suitable partner for the goddess of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer was an early match brand and is also the morning star, the planet Venus.

clue.text: Step, jade green, worn away at edges

indicators.note: the letters at both ends are lost, leaving the inner run

explanation.surface: A stair coloured jade, its edges worn.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is a step on a scale or in a progression.

clue.text: Vamp is about to reform? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, signalling a container
reverses the stated order, so the reform word goes around the little word instead

parts.note: to reform is to improve
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the seductress about to mend her ways?
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the clue would have the short word go round the longer one; 'On the contrary' tells the solver to flip which piece contains which.
explanation.definitionFit: To vamp is to improvise, especially a musical accompaniment made up on the spot.

clue.text: Paramedics initially called to crash

indicators.note: take the first letter of the word

parts.note: rang means telephoned or called

explanation.surface: Ambulance crew first summoned to a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is informal British for a crash, especially of a car or aircraft.

clue.text: Elemental sarcasm

definitions.meaning: made of or like the element iron
mocking language saying the opposite of what is meant

explanation.surface: Basic sarcasm.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means like iron, an element; as a noun, mocking sarcasm.

clue.text: Block off nearby cul-de-sac

definitions.meaning: a dead-end street, often named as such in British addresses

explanation.surface: Seal off the nearby dead-end street.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: the verb shut, the adjective near, and a British name for a dead-end road.

clue.text: Endow part of a hospital

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a section of a hospital with beds

explanation.surface: Fund a section of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To award is to grant, a sense of endow; split, the word is a hospital ward.

clue.text: Love car with top removed for holding party in the open air

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scores, looking like the letter O

indicators.note: the first letter of the car word is taken off

parts.note: auto is a word for a car

indicators.note: the word for keeps the party within it

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A convertible holds a party outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with top removed' takes the A from AUTO, leaving UTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor, or out-of-door, describes something happening in the open air.

clue.text: Showing impatience, say, going back inside too soon

indicators.note: the reversed abbreviation goes within the word for premature

parts.note: early means before the proper time

indicators.note: the abbreviation travels backwards, its letters reversed

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say

explanation.surface: Someone impatiently heads back in before it is time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something eagerly means doing it keenly and impatiently, an adverbial match.

clue.text: Historian city's heard of

indicators.note: the city's name as spoken gives the historian's surname

parts.note: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria in north-west England

explanation.surface: A historian whom the city has heard about.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle was a Scottish historian who wrote The French Revolution.
